entries.text: Let’s walk through Record an explicit outcome. On this slide, use Copy, then Mark done, and leave pending work visible until the external handoff is complete. In practice, a completed acknowledgement proves the transfer step; it does not change White Cell adjudication. Use the highlighted Workflow controls area as your visual reference while you complete this check.

Let’s walk through Draft actions. Translate the room’s decision into a complete action that another reviewer can understand without oral context. Capture intent, instruments, targets, timing, expected effects, assumptions, and rationale before handoff. On this slide, create and revise your team's actions here. Once submitted, they become read-only while White Cell reviews them. In practice, translate the room’s choice into a complete action with enough evidence for the next reviewer to act. Before you continue, verify these points: Strategic Orientation establishes the opening position. Move tabs keep actions attached to the correct round. Submitted or forwarded records become read-only at the documented boundary. When you are ready, use Open actions to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Work the assigned queue. On this slide, inspect both paired outputs and their evidence before recording a specialist decision for the unlocked row. In practice, diplomacy and Information clear together at this specialist boundary; neither track should be silently omitted. When you are ready, use Open assigned queue to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Work the assigned queue. On this slide, work only unlocked NI and Escalation records, checking the six domains and Glasl trajectory against the supplied evidence. In practice, the queue remains dependency-gated. Do not treat a locked row as permission to infer or pre-approve its result. When you are ready, use Open assigned queue to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Proposals. Read the proposal and the complete recipient-specific thread before responding. The first decision opens an isolated negotiation record; later rounds must remain attached to that same thread. On this slide, read proposals White Cell forwarded to this recipient and manage the append-only response thread. In practice, accept, Not Interested, or Negotiate starts the recipient’s isolated thread; later rounds stay attached to it. When you are ready, use Open proposals in Team Action Review to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Read queue state. Start with the badge, pending count, reviewed-history state, and refresh result. Determine whether work is pending, dependency-locked, empty, or already reviewed before opening a card or choosing a decision. On this slide, the queue badge, pending count, reviewed-history controls, and Refresh action show what is ready for this specialist seat. In practice, refresh deliberately when coordinating a handoff; background refresh does not decide an outcome or clear an unread item. Before you continue, verify these points: Pending means the seat still requires action. Locked or empty rows are not approval failures. Reviewed history remains read-only. When you are ready, use Open SME queue to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Population Sentiments. Read the published sentiment as audience-specific scenario context. Identify who received it, what changed in the narrative, and whether the team will respond; do not treat sentiment as a hidden score or automatic outcome. On this slide, review White Cell-published sentiment updates. In practice, sentiment is contextual evidence for participants, not deterministic adjudication. When you are ready, use Open Population Sentiments to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Quick Capture. Record one observable point per capture and label whether it is an observation, moment, or direct quote. Keep interpretation distinct from quoted language and leave formal decisions in the artifact workflow. On this slide, record a concise note, moment, or quote during deliberation. In practice, label the observation accurately and leave formal team decisions in the artifact workflow. When you are ready, use Open Quick Capture to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Transfer approved PLI. On this slide, use Approved PLI to copy finalized specialist JSON into Verba, then acknowledge the packet. In practice, keep the approved specialist payload intact across the external Verba handoff boundary. When you are ready, use Open Approved PLI to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Manage session operations. Keep the selected session stable while moving between settings tabs. Sessions, participants, decks, plugins, and exports are related operational surfaces, but each has a different owner and consequence. On this slide, the Simulation Settings tabs also cover live sessions, participant rosters, facilitator deck assignments, plugins, and export controls. In practice, use the correct tab for the operational task and preserve the current session selection before changing participants, decks, plugins, or exports. Before you continue, verify these points: Sessions establish the active run. Participants and decks determine who can act and what is projected. Plugins and exports remain session-scoped. Use the highlighted Settings tabs area as your visual reference while you complete this check.

Let’s walk through Your role in the exercise. Use this opening step to establish ownership before learning controls. Identify what this seat creates or reviews, what must be handed to another role, and which decisions remain outside your authority. On this slide, as White Cell Support, you operate the control-cell boundary across timing, review, information, and session evidence. In practice, keep deterministic exercise state in the platform, make every review outcome explicit, and leave a chronological record another operator can audit. Before you continue, verify these points: The Lead owns privileged run and review decisions. Support follows the permissions actually exposed to that seat. Participant visibility never substitutes for White Cell review.

Let’s walk through Understand the observer boundary. Begin by separating access from authority. You may inspect the team’s record and follow the exercise, but opening, scrolling, or understanding an item must never change its workflow state. On this slide, this is a read-only view of Green Team's Scribe workspace. In practice, use visibility to understand the exercise, not to assume the authority of an active participant seat. Before you continue, verify these points: Write controls stay hidden or disabled. Opening a record does not change its workflow state.

Let’s walk through Received Proposals. Confirm that the proposal was forwarded to this team, then read its terms and recipient-specific history in full. Interpret the current recipient state from the thread rather than from proposal visibility alone. On this slide, inspect proposals forwarded to this team and their recipient state. In practice, read the full recipient-specific thread before interpreting a proposal outcome. When you are ready, use Open Received Proposals to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Transfer approved PLI. On this slide, use Approved PLI to copy finalized specialist markdown into Tribe Street Journal, then acknowledge the packet. In practice, keep the approved specialist payload intact across the external TSJ handoff boundary. When you are ready, use Open Approved PLI to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Macro PLI. Trace the finalized chain from source action through lever, instrument, implementation assessment, modifiers, citations, and outputs. White Cell consumes this evidence but does not impersonate the specialist who approved or overrode it. On this slide, monitor finalized Macro specialist outputs in read-only form. In practice, the specialist seat owns approval or override. White Cell consumes finalized evidence and must not impersonate the SME decision. When you are ready, use Open Macro PLI to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Inbox. Treat the inbox as incoming context for the Notetaker seat. Open the complete message, decide what it changes in your observation record, and avoid treating receipt of a message as evidence of a team decision. On this slide, read White Cell updates addressed to the Notetaker seat; the badge marks unopened messages. In practice, bring relevant new context into your observation record without treating the inbox itself as a team decision. When you are ready, use Open Inbox to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Team artifacts. Read the orientation, action, or proposal together with its lifecycle label and active exercise context. Observer visibility is evidence of the record, not authority to alter or submit it. On this slide, read Strategic Orientation, actions, or proposals and their current handoff state. In practice, compare the written record with the active exercise context; do not edit or submit it. When you are ready, use Open Team artifacts to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through NI & Escalation PLI. Read the six National Interest domains together with the escalation stage and trajectory. Confirm the Macro dependency cleared before treating downstream output as finalized evidence. On this slide, review finalized National Interest domains and escalation trajectory. In practice, downstream review remains locked until Macro is finalized or explicitly skipped under the workflow contract. When you are ready, use Open NI & Escalation PLI to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Welcome to the Industry Team Facilitator orientation. Guide Industry Team's discussion, review the Scribe handoff, project the working record, and submit the final team artifact to White Cell. Your workflow moves from framing the discussion, to reviewing the Scribe’s record, to projecting and submitting the agreed artifact. Keep presentation, editing, and submission as separate decisions. The team remains responsible for its judgment, while White Cell remains responsible for review.

Let’s walk through Close the loop. Use this checkpoint as a pre-handoff audit. Re-read the active move, required fields, rationale, destination, and lifecycle label; correct the source record before using the explicit handoff control. On this slide, confirm the active move, completeness, rationale, destination, and explicit handoff state before the deadline. In practice, the Scribe owns a trustworthy record, not the team’s strategic judgment and not White Cell’s adjudication. Before you continue, verify these points: Verify the destination before handoff. Use responses and timeline to resolve ambiguity. Collapse Start Here when you need space and reopen it at any time. Use the highlighted Session reference area as your visual reference while you complete this check.

Let’s walk through Timeline. Use chronology to test sequence, identify gaps, and avoid duplicate interpretation. The timeline explains how the session developed; the owning artifact remains authoritative for current workflow state. On this slide, review the chronological session record and the structured snapshots published by manual saves. In practice, use the timeline to check sequence, identify gaps, and avoid duplicating an observation already captured. When you are ready, use Open Timeline to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Welcome to the White Cell Lead orientation. Maintain the authoritative exercise clock, review queues, communications, specialist workflow, and auditable session record without weakening role boundaries. Work through the console as an operator loop: verify shared state, inspect the owning queue, make an explicit decision, communicate it to the intended audience, and confirm the audit trail. Lead and Support must follow the permissions actually exposed to their seats; visibility never grants authority.

Welcome to the Red Team Observer orientation. Follow the team record and exercise state without creating, editing, forwarding, or submitting artifacts. Use this guide to build situational awareness without crossing into participant authority. Follow the record from live context to artifacts, incoming information, and the timeline. At every stop, distinguish what you can inspect from what an active seat is permitted to change.

Let’s walk through Tribe Street Journal. Read or prepare reporting with its source context intact. Distinguish observation, selected quote, scenario reporting, and White Cell publication so participants can judge what kind of evidence they are receiving. On this slide, review published scenario reporting and observations relevant to the team. In practice, use the journal as context; it does not silently change an artifact. When you are ready, use Open Tribe Street Journal to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Welcome to the Industry Team Scribe orientation. Own Industry Team's written decision record, preserve its rationale, and hand complete work across the explicit review boundary. Your workflow moves from listening, to structured drafting, to an explicit handoff. Use each surface to preserve the team’s intent, evidence, assumptions, and rationale. A record is not handed off merely because another role can see it; confirm the documented workflow state before you move on.

Let’s walk through Your role in the exercise. Use this opening step to establish ownership before learning controls. Identify what this seat creates or reviews, what must be handed to another role, and which decisions remain outside your authority. On this slide, as Industry Team Notetaker, you preserve the decision process without interrupting Industry Team's flow. In practice, capture evidence that explains how the room changed: who influenced the choice, where friction emerged, what assumptions shifted, and which moment became decisive. Before you continue, verify these points: Quick captures append to the shared team record. Dynamics and alliance notes remain scoped to your notetaker seat. Manual saves publish structured snapshots to the timeline.

Welcome to the Green Team Notetaker orientation. Preserve how Green Team reached its decisions: the dynamics, alliances, turning points, observations, and sequence behind the formal record. Your walkthrough follows the evidence behind the formal decision. Capture observable moments first, then record dynamics and alliances, compare them with the team artifact, and use the timeline to test whether the sequence is coherent. Preserve your own seat’s perspective without overwriting another observer.

Let’s walk through Team Action Review. Compare the Scribe-forwarded record with the room’s agreed decision. Check completeness, rationale, active move, and lifecycle state, then return to the source artifact for corrections rather than recreating it in the deck. On this slide, review the Scribe-forwarded Strategic Orientation, action, or proposal before final submission. In practice, check completeness, rationale, team agreement, and lifecycle state. Return to the team’s record rather than recreating the artifact in the deck. When you are ready, use Open Team Action Review to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Your role in the exercise. Use this opening step to establish ownership before learning controls. Identify what this seat creates or reviews, what must be handed to another role, and which decisions remain outside your authority. On this slide, as Red Team Facilitator, you keep Red Team's deliberation moving and own the final review boundary. In practice, use the deck to structure the room, inspect what the Scribe forwarded, resolve omissions with the team, and submit only when the artifact represents the agreed decision. Before you continue, verify these points: The Scribe authors and forwards the record. You review, project, and submit it to White Cell. Presentation and submission are separate actions.

Let’s walk through Build proposals. Build the proposal around a named recipient and a clear exchange. Preserve what is offered, what is requested, timing, conditions, and rationale so White Cell and each recipient can understand the same durable record. On this slide, use the Strategic Orientation and move tabs to see exactly what was noted for each part of the simulation. Create and revise your team's proposals here. Once submitted, they become read-only while White Cell reviews them. In practice, translate the room’s choice into a complete proposal with enough evidence for the next reviewer to act. Before you continue, verify these points: Strategic Orientation establishes the opening position. Move tabs keep proposals attached to the correct round. Submitted or forwarded records become read-only at the documented boundary. When you are ready, use Open proposals to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Your role in the exercise. Use this opening step to establish ownership before learning controls. Identify what this seat creates or reviews, what must be handed to another role, and which decisions remain outside your authority. On this slide, as Red Team Notetaker, you preserve the decision process without interrupting Red Team's flow. In practice, capture evidence that explains how the room changed: who influenced the choice, where friction emerged, what assumptions shifted, and which moment became decisive. Before you continue, verify these points: Quick captures append to the shared team record. Dynamics and alliance notes remain scoped to your notetaker seat. Manual saves publish structured snapshots to the timeline.

Welcome to the NI/Escalation SME orientation. Review National Interest domains and escalation evidence after the Macro dependency clears. Treat every queue item as a bounded specialist review. Confirm the source record and dependency state, inspect the complete worksheet or handoff, use the explicit specialist control, and verify the resulting queue state. Your decision becomes evidence for White Cell; it does not replace White Cell’s operational role.

Let’s walk through Tribe Street Journal. Read or prepare reporting with its source context intact. Distinguish observation, selected quote, scenario reporting, and White Cell publication so participants can judge what kind of evidence they are receiving. On this slide, review captures and prepare selected field intelligence for publication. In practice, publish deliberately and preserve the source context so teams can distinguish observation from White Cell inject. When you are ready, use Open Tribe Street Journal to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Timeline. Use chronology to test sequence, identify gaps, and avoid duplicate interpretation. The timeline explains how the session developed; the owning artifact remains authoritative for current workflow state. On this slide, reconstruct when artifacts, RFIs, messages, captures, and updates occurred. In practice, sequence explains how the session developed; the artifact surface remains the source for current workflow state. When you are ready, use Open Timeline to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through PLI Reports. Choose report scope deliberately and confirm all included specialist seats are finalized. Reports summarize existing evidence; generating a report must never create, approve, or alter an adjudication. On this slide, generate session-, move-, or action-scoped reports from finalized specialist outputs. In practice, reports summarize finalized evidence; they do not create or change an adjudication. When you are ready, use Open PLI Reports to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Your specialist boundary. Confirm the queue and decision boundary assigned to this specialist seat. Visibility does not mean an item is ready, and no other operator may approve, override, return, copy, or acknowledge on your behalf. On this slide, as NI/Escalation SME, you own only the review or external handoff assigned to this seat. In practice, use the persisted source evidence, record each outcome explicitly, and leave deterministic exercise decisions with their owning workflow. Before you continue, verify these points: Work only the active session queue. Do not infer missing evidence. Acknowledge external transfers only after the copy step is complete.

Let’s walk through Your role in the exercise. Use this opening step to establish ownership before learning controls. Identify what this seat creates or reviews, what must be handed to another role, and which decisions remain outside your authority. On this slide, as Green Team Scribe, you turn deliberation into the durable Green Team record. In practice, listen for intent, assumptions, and trade-offs; make them legible in Strategic Orientation and proposals before the handoff deadline. Before you continue, verify these points: Draft and revise team-owned artifacts. Preserve rationale and required structured fields. Use the explicit handoff control; visibility alone is not submission.

Let’s walk through Your specialist boundary. Confirm the queue and decision boundary assigned to this specialist seat. Visibility does not mean an item is ready, and no other operator may approve, override, return, copy, or acknowledge on your behalf. On this slide, as Econ SME, you own only the review or external handoff assigned to this seat. In practice, use the persisted source evidence, record each outcome explicitly, and leave deterministic exercise decisions with their owning workflow. Before you continue, verify these points: Work only the active session queue. Do not infer missing evidence. Acknowledge external transfers only after the copy step is complete.

Let’s walk through Green and Industry Proposals. Review each proposal as a recipient-specific workflow. Confirm the intended audience, terms, and White Cell notes before forwarding, and preserve separate append-only threads so one recipient cannot see or alter another recipient’s negotiation. On this slide, review proposals, forward them to named recipients, request changes, or reject them with White Cell notes. In practice, recipient threads remain isolated and append-only so negotiation can be reconstructed. When you are ready, use Open Green and Industry Proposals to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Welcome to the Green Team Facilitator orientation. Guide Green Team's discussion, review the Scribe handoff, project the working record, and submit the final team artifact to White Cell. Your workflow moves from framing the discussion, to reviewing the Scribe’s record, to projecting and submitting the agreed artifact. Keep presentation, editing, and submission as separate decisions. The team remains responsible for its judgment, while White Cell remains responsible for review.

Let’s walk through Team Dynamics. Record the pattern behind the decision: leadership, decision style, friction, consensus, and the move summary. Save when the pattern materially changes or the move closes, preserving your seat-scoped perspective. On this slide, record leadership, decision style, friction, consensus, and a concise move summary. In practice, save when the pattern changes or the move closes. Your seat-scoped notes do not overwrite another Notetaker’s perspective. When you are ready, use Open Team Dynamics to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Blue Actions. Read the complete Blue submission before deciding. Reconcile the active move, structured action fields, rationale, and any requested team notifications; reviewing and sharing are separate operator decisions. On this slide, review Blue Team submissions, accept complete work, or return it with actionable improvement notes. In practice, a completed review changes workflow state explicitly; sharing forward is a separate, deliberate action. When you are ready, use Open Blue Actions to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Responses. Separate White Cell rulings, update notices, forwarded items, and general communications. Bring material information back into the owning team workflow before changing a durable artifact. On this slide, read White Cell answers, update notices, forwarded proposals, and explicit communications. In practice, bring material new information back into deliberation before changing the team record. When you are ready, use Open Responses to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Population Sentiments. Read the published sentiment as audience-specific scenario context. Identify who received it, what changed in the narrative, and whether the team will respond; do not treat sentiment as a hidden score or automatic outcome. On this slide, compose and review team-specific population sentiment updates. In practice, publish the intended audience and narrative explicitly; the update is context, not a hidden score change. When you are ready, use Open Population Sentiments to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Sessions. Create or select the intended run and verify its name and join code before distribution. Preserve archived and inactive sessions as evidence without allowing them to become the accidental live context. On this slide, create the session, assign its join code, select the active run, and preserve the list for operator handoff. In practice, verify the session name and code before distributing access; an archived or different session must not become the accidental live context. When you are ready, use Open Sessions to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Your specialist boundary. Confirm the queue and decision boundary assigned to this specialist seat. Visibility does not mean an item is ready, and no other operator may approve, override, return, copy, or acknowledge on your behalf. On this slide, as TSJ (Tribe Street Journal), you own only the review or external handoff assigned to this seat. In practice, use the persisted source evidence, record each outcome explicitly, and leave deterministic exercise decisions with their owning workflow. Before you continue, verify these points: Work only the active session queue. Do not infer missing evidence. Acknowledge external transfers only after the copy step is complete.

Welcome to the Industry Team Notetaker orientation. Preserve how Industry Team reached its decisions: the dynamics, alliances, turning points, observations, and sequence behind the formal record. Your walkthrough follows the evidence behind the formal decision. Capture observable moments first, then record dynamics and alliances, compare them with the team artifact, and use the timeline to test whether the sequence is coherent. Preserve your own seat’s perspective without overwriting another observer.

Let’s walk through Complete the handoff. Pause before submission and compare the projected discussion with the forwarded source record. Confirm team agreement, active move, completeness, and lifecycle state; projection alone is never submission. On this slide, confirm the Scribe record, the room’s agreement, the active move, and the explicit White Cell submission state. In practice, the Facilitator owns the quality and timing of the handoff; White Cell owns review and adjudication. Before you continue, verify these points: Do not infer submission from projection. Use activity and communications to resolve new inputs. Start Here remains available above the session label. Use the highlighted Session reference area as your visual reference while you complete this check.

Let’s walk through Plugins. Review plugin scope, dependency state, and selected session before changing lifecycle state. A plugin must not silently affect another run or become a substitute for the platform’s deterministic workflow. On this slide, review and manage the plugin lifecycle for the selected session. In practice, confirm scope and dependency state before enabling or disabling a plugin; a plugin must not silently alter another session. When you are ready, use Open Plugins to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through RFIs. Use an RFI when the team needs a ruling, clarification, or missing scenario fact. State one decision-blocking question with enough context to answer, and revise the same record if White Cell returns it. On this slide, send a focused request when the team needs a ruling, clarification, or scenario detail. In practice, include enough context to unblock one decision. If White Cell returns it, revise the same RFI rather than creating a duplicate. When you are ready, use Open RFIs to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through RFIs. Use an RFI when the team needs a ruling, clarification, or missing scenario fact. State one decision-blocking question with enough context to answer, and revise the same record if White Cell returns it. On this slide, answer participant questions or return them with required clarification notes. In practice, keep the answer on the originating RFI so the ruling, revision, and history remain connected. When you are ready, use Open RFIs to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Communications. Use communications for deliberate coordination with a known audience. Verify the recipient and purpose before sending, and keep rulings or requests that require durable workflow history in their owning artifact or RFI surface. On this slide, send injects, announcements, and guidance to all teams, one team, or a specific role. In practice, verify the recipient before sending; broad visibility is an operator choice, not a default. When you are ready, use Open Communications to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Responses. Separate White Cell rulings, update notices, forwarded items, and general communications. Bring material information back into the owning team workflow before changing a durable artifact. On this slide, follow White Cell answers, updates, and inbound operational messages. In practice, treat explicit White Cell responses as exercise input while preserving the observer boundary. When you are ready, use Open Responses to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Record an explicit outcome. On this slide, use the specialist controls to approve, override with an auditable rationale, or send the record back for correction. In practice, keep domain findings and escalation judgment attached to the same reviewed record. Use the highlighted Workflow controls area as your visual reference while you complete this check.

Let’s walk through Your role in the exercise. Use this opening step to establish ownership before learning controls. Identify what this seat creates or reviews, what must be handed to another role, and which decisions remain outside your authority. On this slide, as Red Team Scribe, you turn deliberation into the durable Red Team record. In practice, listen for intent, assumptions, and trade-offs; make them legible in Strategic Orientation and actions before the handoff deadline. Before you continue, verify these points: Draft and revise team-owned artifacts. Preserve rationale and required structured fields. Use the explicit handoff control; visibility alone is not submission.

Let’s walk through Deck. Use the deck to pace and structure the room while keeping the active phase visible. It supports facilitation, but the team artifact remains the durable record and must be reviewed separately. On this slide, move through the assigned support deck and keep the projected discussion aligned to the active exercise phase. In practice, the deck structures facilitation; it is not the durable decision record and does not submit an artifact. When you are ready, use Open Deck to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Quick Capture. Record one observable point per capture and label whether it is an observation, moment, or direct quote. Keep interpretation distinct from quoted language and leave formal decisions in the artifact workflow. On this slide, append observations, key moments, and quotes as separate shared entries. In practice, write one observable point per capture. Distinguish a direct quote from your interpretation and leave formal decisions in the Scribe artifact. When you are ready, use Open Quick Capture to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Welcome to the Red Team Notetaker orientation. Preserve how Red Team reached its decisions: the dynamics, alliances, turning points, observations, and sequence behind the formal record. Your walkthrough follows the evidence behind the formal decision. Capture observable moments first, then record dynamics and alliances, compare them with the team artifact, and use the timeline to test whether the sequence is coherent. Preserve your own seat’s perspective without overwriting another observer.

Let’s walk through RFIs. Use an RFI when the team needs a ruling, clarification, or missing scenario fact. State one decision-blocking question with enough context to answer, and revise the same record if White Cell returns it. On this slide, send a focused question to White Cell or revise the same RFI when it is returned for clarification. In practice, use RFIs for rulings and missing scenario information, not for routine team discussion. When you are ready, use Open RFIs to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Dashboard. Use the dashboard to detect drift, not to resolve it. Compare counts and recent activity with the selected session, then open the owning participant, RFI, session, or export surface before taking action. On this slide, read active sessions, participant counts, pending RFIs, and recent activity at a glance. In practice, use the dashboard to detect operational drift, then open the owning surface before taking action. When you are ready, use Open Dashboard to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Simulation Settings. Treat move, phase, and timer controls as room-level state changes. Confirm operator intent before acting, make one change at a time, and verify the shared tracker immediately afterward. On this slide, advance or reverse moves and phases, start or pause the timer, and reset the clock. In practice, treat every control as a room-level state change. Confirm intent before acting and verify the tracker afterward. When you are ready, use Open Simulation Settings to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Complete the operator loop. Before handoff or export, reconcile shared state, every pending queue, participant access, specialist outputs, communications, and timeline evidence. Record unresolved work explicitly rather than inferring completion from an empty-looking view. On this slide, before handoff or export, reconcile the live tracker, pending queues, participant state, specialist outputs, and timeline. In practice, white Cell owns explicit control and review decisions; specialist seats own their approvals; Game Master owns session administration and evidence export. Before you continue, verify these points: Do not infer completion from visibility. Leave actionable notes when returning work. Start Here remains available above the session label. Use the highlighted Session reference area as your visual reference while you complete this check.

Let’s walk through Activity. Use the activity feed as a triage surface. Open the native destination behind a notice before responding, because the badge tells you that something changed but does not provide the complete decision context. On this slide, review newly submitted records, deck changes, proposal rounds, and White Cell communications. In practice, the badge signals unread activity; opening a notice should take you to its native destination before you act. When you are ready, use Open Activity to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through PLI SME Efficacy. On this slide, review session-level approve and override counts plus the fields specialists change most often. In practice, use the aggregate as a codebook revision signal; it describes specialist outcomes and never changes an individual adjudication. When you are ready, use Open PLI SME Efficacy to move to the live surface. The guide will not make the workflow decision for you.

Let’s walk through Complete the observation loop. Use the formal artifact and your observation record as two complementary views. The artifact states what the team decided; your notes should explain the sequence, influence, friction, and turning points that produced it. On this slide, before the move closes, verify that decisive moments, dynamics, alliances, and the formal artifact tell a coherent story. In practice, the Notetaker explains the process; the Scribe owns the team artifact, the Facilitator owns final handoff, and White Cell owns adjudication.
